$comment: The migrations that have actually been applied to the production Supabase
project (botanique-admin, ref wcacyfyxjiysfibuuhgf).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Vercel deploys the frontend automatically on every
merge to main. Nothing deploys Supabase migrations. PR #98 and PR #99 shipped
frontend code that read fund_releases and fund_acquittals to production while
those tables did not exist there, and the only symptom was a runtime error in
front of the Founder. PR #100 applied the missing migration by hand. This
ledger makes that class of mismatch fail the build instead of the user.
RECONCILE BY NAME, NOT BY VERSION. Supabase stamps its own timestamp when a
migration is applied through the dashboard or MCP, so the hosted version does
not match the repository filename prefix. The name after the prefix is the
stable key, and it is what this ledger and scripts/check-migration-drift.mjs
compare on. `productionVersion` is recorded for traceability only.
HOW TO UPDATE. Only after the migration is genuinely applied to production:
add its entry here, in apply order, with the version Supabase reports for it.
Editing this file does not apply anything — it only records what someone
already did. See docs/ui-authority/operations-hub/MIGRATION-DEPLOYMENT.md.
SPLIT APPLICATION, 12 Aug 2026. project_cost_payments was applied in five
the whole file in one call exceeded the deployment tool's request timeout. The
first attempt timed out and rolled back cleanly, creating nothing — verified
before retrying. The parts were applied in file order, each boundary chosen so
an interrupted run would fail closed: tables and RLS first with no policies or
grants, then functions, then triggers, then policies and grants last. The final
schema was verified object by object and equals the single-file migration.
productionVersion below records the FIRST of those versions.
SPLIT APPLICATION, 12 Aug 2026 (second). project_cost_historical_settlement
was applied in four transactions (versions 20260812203621, 203658, 203729,
203758) for the same reason. The boundaries fail closed: columns, the audit
table and RLS first with no policies or grants; then the settlement functions;
then the payment and cancellation guards; then the read model together with
every policy, revoke and grant. The read model is dropped and recreated to add
a column, so it was deliberately kept in the same transaction as its grant,
leaving no window in which the live register could read an ungranted function.
productionVersion below records the FIRST of those versions.
LOCK ORDER CORRECTION, 13 Aug 2026. project_cost_payment_truth_lock_order
applied cleanly in one transaction (version 20260813105102). It replaces one
function and changes no data: the project_cost_payments content hash, the

CORRECTION-AUTHORITY FIX, 13 Aug 2026.
internal_cost_claim_correction_authority applied cleanly (version
20260813113103). It lets cancel_internal_cost_claim correct an existing
approved Project Cost on a Completed project (a dedicated

totals and the cancelled/approved claim counts were identical before and
after deployment.

filename prefix 20260814090000; production version 20260815192636 —
reconciled by name, not by timestamp, as this file's header explains)
applied cleanly in a single transaction via PR #112 (merge
434482afaa5aebdb389b05b323505c348e137843), byte-identical to the merged-
main file (SHA-256
purely additive: five new tables (maintenance_relationships,
maintenance_relationship_events, maintenance_visits,
maintenance_visit_events, maintenance_assignments), their RLS, indexes,
constraints, triggers and eleven RPCs/helpers. No column was added to
public.projects or public.people, and no existing table, policy, function

STAFF COMPENSATION V1, 16 Aug 2026. staff_compensation_v1 applied cleanly
in one transaction (production version 20260816183349). It is additive and
person-first: Staff Compensation is anchored to public.people, with an optional
Project reference that does not gate the compensation lifecycle. Post-apply
verification confirmed RLS on both new tables, no authenticated direct writes,
and zero Staff Compensation or event rows; no existing operational data was
migrated or rewritten. The performance-advisor follow-up
staff_compensation_v1_indexes applied cleanly in one transaction (production
version 20260816183600), adding only covering indexes for the new requester,
decider and event-actor foreign keys.
STAFF COMPENSATION PAYMENTS V1, 16 Aug 2026. staff_compensation_payments_v1
applied cleanly in one transaction (production version 20260816184658). It
adds Principal-recorded partial/full payment truth, reversal, immutable payment
events, overpayment protection and derived paid/balance status against approved
Staff Compensation only. Project state is never consulted. Post-apply checks
confirmed RLS, no authenticated direct writes, and zero payment/event/position
rows because Staff Compensation itself was still empty. The follow-up
staff_compensation_payment_event_index applied cleanly (production version
20260816184731), adding only the covering payment_id foreign-key index.
STAFF COMPENSATION AUTHORITY + LEGACY TRUTH, 16 Aug 2026.
staff_compensation_authority_and_legacy_truth applied cleanly in one transaction
(production version 20260816201136). It adds Principal direct authorisation
without conflating authorisation with payment, source-claim provenance for
verified legacy imports, and an explicit payment_history_known boundary so
historical approved compensation cannot be displayed as unpaid or accept a new
payment until its old payment position has been reviewed. Three Founder-verified
Martine Lotom legacy staff claims were then imported as canonical Staff
Compensation records with their original Project Costs retained for audit; no
Staff Compensation payment transactions were fabricated.
STAFF COMPENSATION HISTORICAL SETTLEMENT, 17 Aug 2026.
staff_compensation_historical_settlement applied cleanly in one transaction
(production version 20260817090819). It corrects the legacy-payment boundary so
reviewing history can no longer imply KES 0 paid. Imported Staff Pay now stores
a Principal-confirmed historical paid amount separately from dated payment
transactions; effective paid and balance include both, overpayment and
cancellation guards use the combined truth, and a correction returns only the
historical assertion to unconfirmed without deleting real payments. Post-apply
verification confirmed all three imported approved records remained unconfirmed
with KES 0 historical amount as a neutral placeholder; no payment transaction or
historical settlement was fabricated.
MAINTENANCE DAILY SITE EXECUTION, 17 Aug 2026.
maintenance_daily_site_execution applied cleanly in one transaction (production
version 20260817092111). It reuses Daily Site Record as Maintenance's actual
field-execution record: an Active Maintenance relationship keeps a non-archived
site eligible for new Daily Site Records even after implementation stops being
Ongoing. Morning implementation compliance is deliberately unchanged, so weekly
or as-needed Maintenance never creates a false weekday DSR obligation. No
Maintenance relationship, visit, assignment, Project or Daily Site row was
created, changed or backfilled by this migration.
PERSONNEL / LABOUR FINANCE BOUNDARY, 17 Aug 2026.
personnel_labour_finance_boundary applied cleanly in one transaction (production
version 20260817110220). It prevents new Project Cost obligations from using
recipient_type=staff: named Botanique staff belong in Staff Pay, while Project
Cost labour is reserved for casual/site crew. Existing historical staff-labelled
claims remain lifecycle-correctable so withdrawals/cancellations preserve audit
history. Before this boundary was recorded, the duplicate Alego Waweru KES 700
Project Cost was cancelled in favour of its existing Staff Pay record; the
Kitusuru Kefa KES 700 Project Cost remained Withdrawn and a canonical Kefa Staff
Pay record was created. The three Martine imported Staff Pay opening positions
were also Principal-confirmed at KES 0 historically paid, leaving balances of
KES 60,000 Karen, KES 25,000 Alego and KES 30,000 Lugulu.
MAINTENANCE AUTHORITY / ACL CORRECTION, 17 Aug 2026.
maintenance_authority_acl_correction applied cleanly in one transaction
(production version 20260817155812). It aligns Maintenance with the Operations
role model: Principal and Operations Manager have portfolio-wide Maintenance
authority, while Project Team and Read-only remain outside Maintenance V1.
Terminal end-of-service is Principal-only at the RPC boundary and historical
assignment correction remains Principal-only. A read-only production proof
confirmed the Operations Manager sees all three live Maintenance relationships;
an attempted Manager terminal closure was rejected and left the relationship
Active with its version unchanged. The migration changed no operational row.
MAINTENANCE OPERATING LOOP V1, 17 Aug 2026.
maintenance_operating_loop_v1 applied cleanly in one transaction (production
version 20260817181419). It makes the Maintenance visit the operational cycle
around Daily Site Record execution: a completed visit may link to the Accepted
same-site, same-date DSR, records completed/partial outcome and follow-up truth,
and can schedule the next recurring visit in the same transaction. The migration
created no operational rows and auto-closed no visits. Immediately after apply,
the existing Kitusuru and Lugulu 17 Aug visits remained Scheduled with no DSR
link, outcome or follow-up; closure remains an explicit operator action.
MAINTENANCE SERVICE CADENCE V1, 17 Aug 2026.
maintenance_service_cadence_v1 applied cleanly in one transaction (production
version 20260817191907). It added nullable service_days and cadence_end_date
fields plus validation and read-model exposure. The fields are optional only;
they do not create visits or force service dates. The later UI correction keeps
actual Maintenance visits explicitly scheduled so changing client arrangements,
one-off inspections and staff handover periods remain operationally flexible.
MAINTENANCE FOLLOW-UP / SCHEDULING INTEGRITY, 18 Aug 2026.
maintenance_followup_scheduling_integrity applied cleanly in one transaction
(production version 20260818110737). It changes functions only: Active
Maintenance cannot pause while Scheduled visits remain, Paused Maintenance
cannot accept new or rescheduled visits, and derived next_visit_date retains
overdue Scheduled visits instead of reporting them as Not scheduled. No
Maintenance, Project, People, assignment, visit or Daily Site row was changed.
SITE + PROJECT LIFECYCLE FOUNDATION, 18 Aug 2026.
site_project_lifecycle_foundation applied cleanly after one earlier attempt
failed and rolled back before site_id could become NOT NULL. The successful
apply (production version 20260818172640) created durable Site identity, linked
every existing Project to a Site without rewriting Project status/stage truth,
and introduced guarded lifecycle validation for new/deliberate changes. Three
seed-era Projects with null authorship used the active Principal only as the
migration actor on newly created Site rows; Project authorship stayed unchanged.
site_identity_correction (20260818172805) corrected the initial legacy client-
label ambiguity without modifying Project fields. new_project_site_identity
(20260818173318) defines Site / property identity for new Project inserts, and
project_lifecycle_legacy_compatibility (20260818173519) keeps old deprecated
stage rows operationally correctable while rejecting those values on new or
deliberate stage/type changes.
PROJECT ACTIVATION PHASE INTEGRITY, 18 Aug 2026.
project_activation_phase_integrity (production version 20260818182232) closes
the Ongoing + Inquiry path left open when Activate changed status alone.
Inquiry is the pre-active position, so Ongoing and Paused are now rejected
there and activation must name the delivery phase the Project is entering.
Cancelled + Inquiry stays valid, because a Project may be cancelled before it
is ever activated. A read-only check confirmed zero Ongoing/Paused + Inquiry
rows before the guard was applied. Lifecycle enforcement only: no Project,
Site, Maintenance, Staff Pay, Project Cost or Daily Site row was rewritten.
